Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
 Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Tirumala Devi Eada
 L.A.A.S.No.366 of 2014
Judgment:

(per Hon'ble Smt. Justice Tirumala Devi Eada) This appeal, under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, (for short 'the Act') is preferred by the Special Deputy Collector, L.A., Unit-I,
Outer Ring Road Project, HMDA, Tarnaka, Hyderabad aggrieved by the order and decree dated 31.12.2013 passed in L.A.O.P.No.1324 of 2008 by the learned Special Sessions Judge for Trial of Cases under SC's & ST's (POA) Act - cum - VII Additional District & Sessions Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B.Nagar (hereinafter referred to as 'the reference Court').
2. For convenience and clarity, the parties herein are referred to as they were arrayed before the reference Court.

entities.text: SC's & ST's (POA) Act - cum - VII Additional District & Sessions Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B.Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. The facts of the case in brief are that the land to an extent of Ac.22.28 guntas was acquired in Survey Nos.194, 271 to 278 and 281, situated at Shamshabad Village for formation of Outer Ring Road Phase-I, from Gachibowli to Shamshabad.
A draft notification was issued under Section 4(1) of the Act on 24.05.2006 and was published in the Gazette and in the local news papers.

After conducting due enquiry, the Land Acquisition Officer has awarded Rs.1200/- per square yard for non-agriculture lands and AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.366_2014 @ Rs.10,00,000/- per acre was fixed for agricultural lands.

Aggrieved by the said award, the claimants have filed a petition for reference and the same was referred under Section 18 of the Act to the Court of VII Additional District &
Sessions Judge, Ranga Reddy District.

entities.text:
VII Additional District &
Sessions Judge, Ranga Reddy District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
4. The reference Court has framed the following points for consideration:
"1.
Whether the claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as prayed?

2. To what relief?"
5.
Before the reference Court, the claimants got examined PW1 and got marked Exs.A1 and A2.
On behalf of the respondents, RW1 was examined and Ex.B1 was marked.

sentences.text: Based on the evidence on record, the reference Court has enhanced the compensation to Rs.1200/- per square yard for the acquired lands, apart from the other statutory benefits.
Aggrieved by the said enhancement, the Special Deputy Collector has preferred the present appeal.
7. Heard the submissions of Smt.D.Madhavi, learned Standing Counsel for the appellant and Sri A.Pulla Reddy, learned counsel for the respondents.
AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.366_2014 8.

Learned counsel for the appellant has argued that the reference Court has viewed the entire case in a wrong perspective and that it has failed to appreciate the evidence on record and that the compensation was enhanced without any rationale.

She further argued that the reference Court has committed an error by relying on Ex.A1, as no person connected with the said document was examined and that the property under Ex.A1 is situated in a different survey number.

Learned counsel further contended that the extent of land covered under Ex.A1 is only 3,402 square yards which cannot be compared with that of large extent that is acquired in the present proceedings i.e.
Ac.17.14  guntas.
Therefore, prayed to set aside the award passed by the reference Court and confirm the award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer.

9. The respondents counsel, on the other hand, has submitted that the total lands that were acquired had high potential and that there are many layouts and ventures coming along the ring road and that the acquired lands would fetch more than what is awarded by the reference Court.

He therefore,
prayed to dismiss the appeal.

10. Based on the above rival contentions, this Court frames the following points for consideration:
AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.366_2014 1.
Whether the claimants are not entitled for enhancement of compensation?
2. Whether the order and decree of the trial Court need any interference?

3. To what relief?
11. POINT NO.1:
a) A perusal of Ex.A1 shows that M/s.Indu Projects Limited as a GPA holder of Smt.Jasoda bai Bhangdiya, has sold the property on 09.9.2005 in favour of M/s.Shell India Marketing Private Ltd., admeasuring 3402.78 Sq.yards in survey No.674 (part)
situated at Shamshabad village for a consideration of Rs.3,60,00,000/-, which comes to Rs.10582/- per square yard.
b) PW1 is the first claimant.

His evidence reveals that the acquired lands are abutting the NH-7 leading from Hyderabad to Bangalore and that they have a potential for The Special Deputy Collector vs M.Pratap Reddy on 6 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126520954/
2 usage of commercial purposes and that it is in the vicinity of International airport.

entities.text: Special Deputy Collector vs M.Pratap Reddy on 6 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further deposed about the sale transaction under Ex.A1 and that the said transaction was prior to the date of acquisition.

He further submitted that they have purchased the acquired land with a fond hope of constructing commercial complexes in future but since, they have been acquired, they need to be compensated and that the amount awarded by the LAO is very meager.
But for making mere suggestions that were denied, nothing material could be elicited during his cross examination to discredit his evidence.

AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.366_2014 He has also relied upon Ex.A2 which is a copy of decree in LAOP No.702 of 2010, wherein the reference Court has granted compensation of Rs.5,500/- per square yard, for the land at Shamshabad that was acquired by the Special Deputy Collector Unit-I,
ORR project HUDA.

c) RW1 who is the Land acquisition Officer has admitted during his cross examination that the land is facing the National Highway leading from Hyderabad to Bangalore and that it was developed as plots by Sama Enclave for residential purposes and that there is a HUDA colony at Shamshabad prior to the notification of the present acquisition.
He further admitted that Ex.A1, the sale deed was referred in the award but was not considered stating that it relates to the transaction which is prior to the notification.
d) Thus, it is elicited through RW1 that the lands that are acquired have high potential and that they are very near to the Shamshabad Airport and also the National Highway.
The transaction under Ex.A1 was referred in the sales statistics under Ex.B1 but he has not taken into consideration, which is not proper.
The sale is dated 09.09.2005 while the notification is dated 24.05.2006.
The sale statistics which fall within three years prior to notification are to be considered while awarding compensation.
AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.366_2014 e)

In this regard, it is apt to refer to a decision of the Apex Court in Ram Kanwar v. State of Haryana 1 and in Mehrawal Khewaji Trust v. State of Punjab 2, it is held as under:
"When there are several exemplars with reference to similar lands, it is the general rule that the highest of the exemplars, if it is satisfied that it is a bona fide transaction, has to be considered and accepted."

entities.text: Ram Kanwar v. State of Haryana 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Mehrawal Khewaji Trust v. State of Punjab 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
f) In P.Ram Reddy v. Land Acquisition Officer, Hyderabad 3, the High Court of Andhra Pradesh opined that "Normally we have to take into consideration the sales of three years prior to the notification".
g) Further, in Ravindar Narain and another v. Union of India 4, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that the principles for fixation of market value with reference to comparable sales have to be followed to minimize speculation and the requisites for a sale to merit consideration as a comparable sale were The Special Deputy Collector vs M.Pratap Reddy on 6 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126520954/
3 held as follows:-
"1) When sale is within a reasonable time of the date of notification under Section 4 (1) of Land Acquisition Act,
2) It should be a bona fide transaction,
3) It should be of the land acquired or of the land adjacent to the land acquired, and 4) It should possess similar advantages."
(2020) 17 SCC 232 (2012) 5 SCC 432 1993(2) LAT 1 (2003) 4 SCC 481 AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.366_2014 h) In the present case, the sale is within a reasonable time i.e. within one year and the land is said to be in the close proximity to the acquired land and also there is no dispute about the transaction under Ex.A1 with regard to its genuineness and it is already brought on record that RW1 has admitted that the acquired land has high potential.
i) Thus, the oral evidence of the claimants coupled with the exhibits, it is held that the reference Court is justified in enhancing the compensation to Rs.1200/- per square yard for the acquired lands, apart from the other statutory benefits.
j) It is further contended by the appellant counsel that the lands of small units cannot be taken as comparable statistics while awarding compensation to larger extents.
k) It is relevant to refer to the judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Land Acquisition Officer,
Revenue Divisional Officer v. L.Kamalamma 5 and Trishala Jain v. State of Uttaranchal 6.
l)

sentences.text:
In Land Acquisition Officer, Revenue Divisional Officer's case (supra 3), the Hon'ble Apex Court held as under:
"6. ...when no sales of comparable land were available where large chunks of land had been sold, even land transactions in respect of smaller extent of land could be taken note of as indicating the price that it may fetch in respect of large tracts (1998) 2 Supreme Court Cases 385 (2011) 6 SCC 47 AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.366_2014 of land by making appropriate deductions such as for development of the land by providing enough space for roads, sewers, drains, expenses involved in information of a layout, lump sum payment as also the waiting period required for selling the sites that would be formed".
m) In Trishala Jain v. State of Uttaranchal's case (supra 4), the Hon'ble Apex Court held as under:
The Special Deputy Collector vs M.Pratap Reddy on 6 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126520954/
4

entities.text: (1998) 2 Supreme Court Cases 385 (2011) 6 SCC 47 AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.366_2014
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Trishala Jain v. State of Uttaranchal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "The sale instances even of smaller plots could be considered for determining the market value of a larger chunk of land with some deduction unless, there was comparability in potential, utilization, amenities and infrastructure with hardly any distinction.
On such principles each case would have to be considered on its own merits".

n) Thus, when no other comparable documents are available, the sale transactions involving smaller extents of land can be considered by allowing reasonable deductions, if they are similar in potentiality, utilization, amenities and infrastructure.
Based on the said principle, the reference Court has enhanced the compensation to Rs.1200/- per square yard for the acquired lands, apart from the other statutory benefits.

o) In view of the foregoing discussion, it is held that the compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer is very meager and the enhancement made by the reference Court to the extent of Rs.1200/- per square yard, apart from the other statutory benefits, is well justified.
Point No.1 is answered accordingly.
AKS,J & ETD,J LAAS No.366_2014 12. POINT NO.2:
In view of the reasoned finding arrived at Point No.1, this Court holds that order and decree of the reference Court do not need any interference.
13. POINT NO.3:

In the result, the appeal is dismissed upholding the order and decree dated 31.12.2013 passed in L.A.O.P.No.1324 of 2008 by the learned Special Sessions Judge for Trial of Cases under SC's & ST's (POA) Act - cum - VII Additional District &
Sessions Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B.Nagar.
